policy.sectionsRead: Word metadata and quiz guidance, lines 138-176
facts: Word title is the meaning-quiz label. Exclusions are direct symmetric pairs applied in both language directions, not transitive closure.
The criterion is whether a learner could reasonably accept the competing title, not merely whether two words describe the same scene.
The current RU instructions require checking Russian polysemy, secondary Japanese senses and actual caption components; primary readings or the card body do not necessarily constrain the bare quiz.
The current RU instructions explicitly distinguish conservative dictionary-supported protection from a claim of contemporary frequency or ordinary-quiz necessity.
policy.directionConvention: Each pair has two language directions and two possible target cards. The eight matrix rows below make those cases explicit. A symmetric implementation rule does not imply symmetric linguistic evidence.

provenance.restrictedSources: Gramota/BTS/orthographic dictionary and Kotobank are cited by URL, named dictionary, headword and section. evidence.dictionary: Русский орфографический словарь, edited by V. V. Lopatin and O. E. Ivanova, via Gramota
evidence.locator: First exact headword result; distinguish nominal entry 2 from adverb entry 1 and the following далеко не entry. Do not use the generic Metadictionary panel below as a substitute.
evidence.observation: The entry explicitly indexes a declinable nominal homograph covering spatial remoteness. Both stress/spelling variants are admitted, with genitives in -а. It is not limited to the future, and the variant spelled with е is explicitly present.
evidence.proves: The exact unaccented project string далеко can identify a noun, not only an adverb or predicate. No conversion of е into ё is necessary to obtain this reading.
evidence.doesNotProve: No Japanese equivalent is supplied. This is not a frequency measure or proof that a learner will choose that reading inside either full semicolon-separated caption.
evidence.confidence: high for the attested nominal spelling and spatial sense

evidence.dictionary: Большой толковый словарь русского языка, S. A. Kuznetsov (chief editor), via Gramota
evidence.locator: Nominal subentry after adverb/predicate sections I-II and before далеко за
evidence.observation: A neuter nominal subentry is marked colloquial. Its coverage includes a remote place where someone is situated as well as future reference. It gives a location-use example and attributes a second example to Gogol.
evidence.proves: Positive Russian lexical support for the remote-location noun reading; the older all-adverb analysis of the caption string is incomplete.
evidence.doesNotProve: No Japanese translation, present-day frequency, unrestricted replacement of distance adverbs or adjective, or ordinary-quiz necessity.
evidence.independence: Different named dictionary from R1, hosted on the same site; not presented as an independent corpus sample.
evidence.confidence: high for lexical attestation; no frequency conclusion

evidence.author: Nikolai Gogol
evidence.work: Dead Souls, volume I, chapter XI
evidence.quote: Русь! Русь! вижу тебя, из моего чудного, прекрасного далека тебя вижу
evidence.observation: The preposition and agreeing modifiers accompany an inflected nominal form. This is an actual attributed use, not an invented teaching example.
evidence.proves: Historical nominal usage denoting the speaker's remote vantage/location.
evidence.doesNotProve: Modern frequency, the nominative spelling by itself (use R1/R2 for the paradigm), Japanese translation or ordinary bare-quiz acceptability.
evidence.confidence: high for the text observed; qualified by unproofread transcription

entries.quote: на большом расстоянии либо на большое расстояние

entries.locator: Russian небо I, meanings 1-2 and translation table
entries.description: Sky/overhead space and religious heaven; the Japanese translation table lists 天 and 空/そら. This community entry is not an exhaustive denial of other meanings.

evidence.observation: These support ordinary adverbial/adjectival readings, but the inspected Wiktionary далеко page does not supply R1/R2's noun. That incompleteness must not be used to erase the noun attested in the named dictionaries.

entries.description: Adverbial distance and a construction with от plus a reference point; examples retain that construction.
Attribute/predicate of spatial or temporal distance and additional figurative senses; its short neuter form is a separate reason not to assume every далеко occurrence is an adverb.

Includes sky/airspace, a homeland/foreign-land symbolism within the sky section, and religious uses. The locality examples have modifying material or prepositions; this does not establish bare небо as an equivalent of a generic remote location.

entries.dictionary: Большой универсальный словарь русского языка, V. V. Morkovkin, G. F. Bogacheva, N. M. Lutskaya
entries.description: The inspected named entry includes locative phraseology involving под plus specified territory. A geographic construction is not an independent bare caption equivalence.

evidence.doesNotProve: No negative impossibility result. These controls block a simplistic inference from sky being far away, or from phrase-level homeland symbolism, to bare lexical equivalence.

evidence.coverage: Full entries for these four IDs and 1245280 空/から were printed and read. The excerpted senses above are the ones relevant to this proposal.
evidence.doesNotProve: No Russian translation supplied; no English-to-Russian gloss chaining alone establishes C2.

evidence.dictionary: デジタル大辞泉, Shogakukan, via Kotobank
evidence.description: The remote-place sense relates a location to someone's home/base and also extends to circumstance. Its examples concern a foreign country, travel and remembered home. No Russian equivalent is present.
evidence.proves: The Japanese noun has a genuinely locational reading, not only the optical sky sense.
evidence.doesNotProve: No universal N+の空 restriction or blanket literary label is stated for this sense. The displayed examples do not independently settle bare quiz acceptability.

evidence.proves: An actual Russian sky rendering paired with 空/そら.
evidence.limitation: Russian based_on_id points to an Esperanto sentence. The Japanese link is direct in the translation graph, not direct-translation authorship. No remote-place sense is tested.

japanese.text: 遠くに富士山が見えた。

evidence.proves: Attested Russian вдали for Japanese 遠くに in a complete sentence; Russian creation metadata names this Japanese source sentence.
evidence.limitation: Supports the existing caption, not a standalone 空 equivalence.

evidence.proves: Attested Russian predicative далеко for Japanese 遠い in a complete sentence.
evidence.limitation: Russian creation metadata points to English, not Japanese. Does not support a remote-location noun reading of 遠い or 空.

authorAnalysis.newBridge: R1-R3 establish positive Russian evidence for a remote-location noun whose unaccented nominative is exactly далеко. J1/J2 establish a Japanese remote-place noun sense of 空/そら. Comparing those meanings is this author's bilingual semantic adjudication, NOT a direct Japanese-Russian dictionary quotation or an attested translation of Gogol.
authorAnalysis.proposal: Both pairs now have a concrete, non-transitive basis for considering a conservative direct exclusion through the shared literal caption component далеко, read as the attested noun. This is a review proposal, not accepted C2 or authority to add it.
authorAnalysis.proposalConfidence: medium for conservative caption-overlap judgment; high for the underlying lexical facts
limits: There is still no newly verified bilingual source rendering standalone 空 as the Russian noun далеко.
No source here establishes bare 空 as the ordinary Russian adverb далеко, adverb вдали or adjective далёкий.
No contemporary corpus frequency, learner-confusion rate or ordinary-quiz necessity has been established.

The full caption neighbours вдали and далёкий strongly suggest the usual distance readings. Whether that contextual cue sufficiently excludes the nominal homograph is a real adjudication question, not decided by orthography alone.
No new finding says Japanese 空 and 遠い are generally interchangeable or that the Russian adjective means a remote place.
Russian sky/locality phraseology is not proof that bare небо is a good caption for 遠く or 遠い.
Earlier qualified review 004 is preserved, not retroactively called wrong: the Russian noun evidence was not part of that record.
